tasks.task:
Plan a new module: Thrum's game SDK, the public interface game developers and coding agents use to build new games.

The owner's request, in their words: "What I would like you to plan is a high end, intuitive, expressive, readable, SDK that game developers can use to build new games. this should be what V1 uses ideally and what we will use to build the swarm game. It's VITAL that we get this right as it's the entire interface that developers and coding agents will use to build a variety of games. It's the front of the product we're building. So it needs to be as intuitive, well documented and easy to use as possible."

The owner's decisions (25 Nov 2026), in their words: "V1 first, Rust only, I'll approve the design."
- V1 first: the V1 exit does not wait for the SDK. V1 lands on today's API; SDK work packages then move the showcase (examples/v1-game) onto the SDK, and the swarm game (docs/design/NEXT-GOAL-SWARM-GAME.md) is built on it from the start. Order the SDK's dependencies so no V1-path work package (APPLE-PRESENTATION WP8-WP12, SHOWCASE WP7-WP8, RAY-TRACING WP6, GAME-SPLIT WP4, MESH-SHADING WP3) waits on it.
- Rust only: games are written in Rust. No scripting layer.
- The owner approves the SDK design before any builder starts. Say so in the design and plan, and end your report with what the owner should look at to approve it.

Outcome: a developer or agent who has never seen Thrum builds a small 3D game, a small 2D game and a networked game from the SDK's documentation alone, and the code reads as plainly as the game it describes. One structure and one vocabulary across 2D, 3D, single-player and multiplayer; good-looking defaults; mistakes that explain themselves; every public item documented with an example. The SDK is the front door over the engine's existing modules (render, atmosphere, controls, assets and hot reload, profiler, GAME-UI, RENDER-2D, SESSION, TRANSPORT, sim2d); it does not leak their internals, and it keeps the hardware-native performance policy (docs/design/AI-PERFORMANCE.md, docs/design/decisions/HARDWARE-NATIVE-ENGINE.md).

What the design must settle and show: the game structure (app, scenes, entities/objects, systems or behaviours), the lifecycle against the fixed tick and the frame host, input actions, the scene and rendering surface, assets, UI, 2D and 3D under one model, multiplayer as an opt-in, errors, and documentation (reference, guides, templates). Show it with worked examples: real games written against the proposed API (at least the swarm game's core loop, a slice of the V1 showcase and a small starter), so the owner judges the API by reading game code. Research how current engines and frameworks do this (for example Bevy, Godot, Unity, Unreal, Fyrox, macroquad) and choose by what serves Thrum best, with your reasons; prefer modern, state-of-the-art approaches. Physics, animation and audio: say whether they belong in this module's first release, and bring that to the owner as a decision rather than assuming.

Pointers: the existing SDK ambition and creator path in docs/design/ENGINE-EXPERIENCE.md, FIRST-USE-WALKTHROUGHS.md, FROM-SCRATCH-WALKTHROUGHS.md, SCENARIO-WALKTHROUGHS.md and ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md (evidence to judge, not a template); the CREATOR and GAME-SPLIT modules, which overlap and must be reconciled in the module list; the C4 contracts in docs/design/CONTRACTS.md; .config/architecture.toml for crate registration. Use the glossary's terms and propose new names where needed.
The design review of GAME-SDK at .orchestrate/evidence/GAME-SDK/design-review.md asked for changes, with its 15 Must Fix findings.

The design review of GAME-SDK at .orchestrate/evidence/GAME-SDK/design-review.md asked for changes, with its 5 Must Fix findings. That makes 2 design reviews in a row that asked for changes, so the script approves the design you leave without another review, and building starts from it. Also record an owner decision, 25 November 2026: asked whether the first release should keep the planner's default (2D queries and sprite animation in; rigid bodies, skeletal animation and audio out) or add physics and audio, the owner answered "Planner's default". Write it into the design and plan as decided rather than open, and remove it from what is left for the owner. The owner still approves the whole design before any work package is built.

Rewrite the GAME-SDK design (docs/plans/GAME-SDK/DESIGN.md, and PLAN.md/DONE.json to match) as the best SDK we can design. The owner, 26 Nov 2026: "We're looking for something that's readable, expressive, intuitive and powerful. Don't optimise at all for reducing the amount of re-work needed. Let's just find the best possible design."

Inputs (absolute paths; these are outside Git, read them from the main checkout):
1. /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum/.orchestrate/evidence/GAME-SDK/owner-review-2026-11-26.md — industry review. The owner answered "Yes I agree" to ALL ten recommendations and ALL four owner decisions (input-only cross-device replay with floats for presentation; Rust prefabs, typed assets and children, no editor; the first character is a player's, predicted against fixed 2D scenery, entering the standard lobby; typed content IDs from day one, versioned saves and data packs as year-one commitments). These are decided: write them into the design as decisions.
2. Three dogfood reports, where agents wrote full games against the design as amended by that review:
   /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum/tmp/sdk-dogfood/arena-3d-online/REPORT.md (online 3D arena shooter)
   /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum/tmp/sdk-dogfood/platformer-2d/REPORT.md (2D precision platformer)
   /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum/tmp/sdk-dogfood/explorer-3d/REPORT.md (3D third-person exploration)
   Their game source with inline `// SDK:` notes is beside each report. All three said "not yet, I'd pick Godot/Unity", and all three praised the same core (written rule order, the rule/frame type wall, phases, windowless tests).

What done looks like:
- Every ambiguity the dogfooders had to guess at is resolved with a named type and signature (phase change/read, scene restart and arguments, prefab declaration and overrides, typed content end to end, saves into and out of a running game, test harness entity lookup, Num literal rules on one page and the float types frame code sees, where `control` runs in the rule order).
- The recurring friction is designed out: a controlled-character function that can read settings, phase and events (state plainly which parameters cost prediction); a character move against level collision that reports contacts; teleport/cut for interpolation; pause; runtime parenting; local-only keys and pointer for frame functions; level/tile collision that content chosen at run time can load; bots as players; richer roster.
- Worked examples rewritten so each reads as the best code a developer could write in this SDK, covering the 2D, 3D and online cases.
- Scope: the owner's first-release scope (2D queries and sprite animation in; rigid bodies, skeletal animation, audio out; 3D multiplayer out) stands unless the owner changes it. Where the reports show a genre is blocked by a scope line (3D collision queries and character move, gamepad, audio, predicted projectiles, lag compensation), design the API shape anyway so it fits, and put each first-release scope change as a one-line owner question with your recommendation in a clearly marked section. Do not decide those yourself.
- Rust only. The owner approves the design before any build, so do not start a builder.
